public_rationale: On June 9, 2026, AWS announced Fable 5 availability on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS, describing it as a Mythos-class model with safeguards [e1]. Specified harmful requests were routed to Opus 4.8, while Mythos 5 without those limits remained restricted to vetted customers [e1]. This supports the contextual claim that Anthropic released a safeguarded Mythos-class version by June 9 [e1].
limitations: Support depends on interpreting Marcus's reference to Mythos as including the safeguarded Fable 5 version.
The announcement does not establish immediate access for every account or region.
The evidence does not independently establish safeguard effectiveness or measure the engineering effort involved.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic added some guardrails to Mythos and released it.

statement.excerpt: Instead, Anthropic tacked some guardrails on, and pushed it out the door.

from_speaker: Anyone can now use it, for the right price
our_interpretation: Read in context, the factual commitment is that Anthropic added safeguards to a Mythos-class model and made the guarded version generally available by June 9.
This allows a safeguarded version with a different product name; it does not require the unchanged April preview or unrestricted Mythos 5 to become public.
Tacked some guardrails on does not supply a testable claim about the engineering effort or effectiveness of those safeguards.
criteria.support_condition: Primary release records establish general availability by June 9 of a Mythos-class model with added technical or deployment safeguards.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Primary records establish that no safeguarded Mythos-class model had been generally released by June 9, or that the released model was unrelated to Mythos.
